contraindications: Haloperidol and other high-potency D2 antagonists (class warning): severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions are reported in anti-NMDAR encephalitis.
interactions: Methylprednisolone: lowers potassium further (current potassium 3.0 mmol/L) and raises glucose; replace potassium and monitor.
Aciclovir IV with fluid restriction for hyponatraemia: aciclovir needs adequate hydration to avoid crystal nephropathy; give it in isotonic saline and monitor creatinine.
IVIG: can lower measured sodium (pseudohyponatraemia from the protein load) and carries thrombotic and renal risks; interpret sodium with serum osmolality.
Lorazepam + levetiracetam: additive sedation; monitor consciousness and breathing.
output.proposed: IV aciclovir, IV methylprednisolone, IVIG, levetiracetam and lorazepam; no regular home medications
output.summary: No interaction prevents the planned therapy. Steroids worsen the low potassium; aciclovir needs isotonic fluid despite the fluid restriction; IVIG can lower the measured sodium.
warnings: Screen for hepatitis B (HBsAg, anti-HBc) before any rituximab dose.
Amoxicillin allergy (rash): avoid penicillins; a cephalosporin such as cefazolin is acceptable for surgical prophylaxis after a non-severe rash.

output.query: ovarian teratoma in anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis: diagnosis and treatment

results.finding: Definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis requires one or more of six major symptom groups and IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies, with CSF testing included; probable disease requires four groups (or three with a teratoma) of rapid onset plus an abnormal EEG or CSF pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands.
results.source: Graus F et al. Lancet Neurol 2016;15:391-404

results.finding: All patients had antibodies in CSF, whereas about 14% were negative in serum; CSF titres related more closely to outcome than serum titres.
results.source: Gresa-Arribas N et al. Lancet Neurol 2014;13:167-177

results.finding: 38% had a tumour, mostly ovarian teratoma; 53% improved within 4 weeks of first-line immunotherapy or tumour removal; second-line rituximab or cyclophosphamide after first-line failure was associated with better outcome; 81% had mRS 0-2 at 24 months.
results.source: Titulaer MJ et al. Lancet Neurol 2013;12:157-165

results.finding: Ovarian teratomas are the main associated tumour; prompt tumour removal together with immunotherapy is associated with faster improvement and fewer relapses.
results.source: Dalmau J et al. Lancet Neurol 2011;10:63-74

output.summary: Published criteria and cohort data on anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis: definite diagnosis rests on CSF IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies; first-line immunotherapy and tumour removal are followed by second-line agents when there is no response.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum anti-GluN1 positive (1:1024); sodium 124 mmol/L (profound hyponatraemia) with potassium 3.0 mmol/L; thyroid function, thyroid antibodies and other neuronal antibodies negative; beta-hCG negative
action_criteria.label: Obtain the reviewed serum work-up, including a cell-based IgG anti-GluN1 assay that must be interpreted with CSF rather than alone
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes metabolic, endocrine, toxic and infective mimics, shows the hyponatraemia and gives the serum anti-GluN1 result, which is read with the CSF assay.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Symmetric bilateral medial temporal and subtle putaminal FLAIR hyperintensity without restricted diffusion, haemorrhage or enhancement; no structural lesion
action_criteria.label: Obtain contrast-enhanced brain MRI to exclude HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination; a normal MRI does not exclude anti-NMDAR encephalitis
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination before LP; it is normal in most patients and does not confirm the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Lymphocytic pleocytosis (76 cells/uL), protein 92 mg/dL, 7 CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands and IgG index 1.18; HSV PCR negative; CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (1:64) on cell-based assay
action_criteria.label: Analyze CSF for cells, protein and glucose, OCB/IgG index, HSV PCR and a cell-based IgG anti-GluN1 assay interpreted in parallel with serum
action_criteria.rationale: CSF anti-GluN1 IgG on a cell-based assay is the decisive test for definite disease, and HSV PCR addresses the can't-miss infectious mimic.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Extreme delta brush and two right temporal electrographic seizures on a slow background
action_criteria.label: Obtain EEG for encephalopathic and epileptiform abnormalities, explicitly assessing for extreme delta brush
action_criteria.rationale: Staring spells, a convulsive seizure, dyskinesias and fluctuating alertness need an EEG to separate seizures from movements; an abnormal EEG supports the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Bilateral ovarian mature cystic teratomas (right 3.2 cm, left 2.4 cm) with preserved ovarian tissue
action_criteria.label: Screen for an ovarian teratoma with pelvic and abdominal ultrasound
action_criteria.rationale: Women of reproductive age carry the highest teratoma risk; tumour removal is part of first-line treatment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Seizure burden and evolution of the background over 24 hours or more
action_criteria.label: Escalate to continuous EEG monitoring for seizure burden and non-convulsive seizures
action_criteria.rationale: Two electrographic seizures on a routine EEG with fluctuating alertness: continuous EEG measures the seizure burden.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum osmolality 258 mOsm/kg with urine osmolality 460 mOsm/kg and urine sodium 52 mmol/L, normal thyroid function and cortisol
action_criteria.label: Work up the profound hyponatraemia with serum and urine osmolality
action_criteria.rationale: Sodium 124 mmol/L after poor oral intake needs serum and urine osmolality and urine sodium to separate SIADH from hypovolaemia before fluid restriction.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Steroid effect on the low potassium, aciclovir hydration against fluid restriction, IVIG effect on measured sodium
action_criteria.label: Check interactions between the planned treatment and the current medication list
action_criteria.rationale: She takes no regular medicines, so the check is optional; the planned drugs' effects on potassium and fluid balance are covered by the musts.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General published evidence on anti-NMDAR encephalitis diagnosis and immunotherapy
action_criteria.label: Optionally consult the published evidence on anti-NMDAR encephalitis diagnosis and immunotherapy
action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; no diagnostic or management step depends on it.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give haloperidol or other high-potency D2 antagonists for agitation: patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis are prone to severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions.
Do not delay immunotherapy while waiting for the anti-NMDAR antibody result when clinical probability is high: antibody turnaround can take 1-2 weeks and delay worsens outcome.
Do not attribute the presentation to a primary psychiatric disorder while seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF inflammation remain unexplained.
Do not perform lumbar puncture without prior imaging in a patient with altered consciousness, focal signs, or new seizures: exclude mass effect first.
Do not interpret a negative serum anti-NMDAR antibody as ruling out the disease; the CSF assay is the gold standard and may be positive when serum is negative.
Do not perform bilateral oophorectomy when ovary-sparing resection is feasible.
required_recommendations: Start IV aciclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 hours at presentation, and stop it once CSF HSV PCR is negative and the antibody diagnosis is established; repeat the PCR on a second CSF sample if the first LP was within 72 hours of onset and HSV encephalitis remains plausible.

Start first-line immunotherapy without waiting for the antibody result once infection is reasonably excluded: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days with IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total) or plasma exchange (5 to 7 exchanges).
Arrange prompt laparoscopic removal of both ovarian teratomas, with ovary-sparing cystectomy where feasible, as part of first-line treatment, with gynaecology.
Treat seizures with an antiseizure medication such as levetiracetam or lacosamide; avoid valproate in a woman able to become pregnant; seizures respond mainly to immunotherapy.
Monitor with continuous EEG for non-convulsive seizures while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist.

Admit to the ICU / neurocritical care for autonomic instability (heart rate 138 bpm, blood pressure 172/108 mmHg, diaphoresis, fever), SpO2 94% with respiratory rate 24, seizures and profound hyponatraemia, with airway assessment and cardiac monitoring.

If there is no meaningful clinical improvement 10 to 14 days after first-line therapy, escalate to rituximab (375 mg/m² weekly for 4 doses or 1 g twice 2 weeks apart, after hepatitis B screening) and/or cyclophosphamide; discuss fertility preservation before cyclophosphamide.
Treat agitation and insomnia with benzodiazepines (lorazepam) first.

Treat the profound hyponatraemia (124 mmol/L) as SIADH once hypovolaemia is excluded: fluid restriction, with a hypertonic (3%) saline bolus for seizures, correcting by no more than 10 mmol/L in 24 hours; give IV aciclovir in isotonic saline rather than free water.
Replace potassium (3.0 mmol/L) and recheck it during high-dose corticosteroids.

Assess nutrition after the 6 kg weight loss from refusal to eat, and start nasogastric feeding if intake stays poor, with refeeding precautions (thiamine, phosphate, potassium and magnesium monitoring).
Neurology-led care with psychiatry for behavioural management; gynaecology for the teratomas.

avoided_actions.rationale: Transthoracic echo is not indicated for anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it adds cost without informing diagnosis or management unless a discrete cardiac concern (e.g., new murmur, embolic stroke) coexists.
EMG/NCS plays no role in the diagnostic workup of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it neither confirms the antibody-mediated CNS process nor distinguishes among the differential diagnoses.
Amyloid PET targets Alzheimer pathology and contributes no information to the diagnosis or treatment of autoimmune encephalitis in a young patient with subacute neuropsychiatric symptoms.

DaTscan evaluates nigrostriatal dopaminergic function and has no role in autoimmune encephalitis; the orofacial dyskinesias of anti-NMDAR encephalitis are antibody-mediated, not presynaptic dopaminergic.

differential.key_features: CSF HSV PCR negative on an LP about 2 weeks after onset; MRI medial temporal signal symmetric, without haemorrhage or restricted diffusion; the febrile illness 4 weeks earlier resolved without encephalopathy; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.

differential.diagnosis: Other antibody-mediated encephalitis (anti-LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B or AMPA receptor)
differential.key_features: Serum neuronal-surface panel negative (LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B, AMPA) and onconeural antibodies negative; the hyponatraemia does not make LGI1 encephalitis likely with CSF anti-GluN1 positive.
Seizures, orofacial dyskinesias and choreoathetosis, autonomic instability, extreme delta brush and CSF pleocytosis with oligoclonal bands are not explained by a psychiatric disorder.

differential.diagnosis: Drug-induced psychosis or neuroleptic malignant syndrome
differential.key_features: No substance or antipsychotic exposure; urine drug screen negative; CK only 342 U/L with dyskinesias and seizures.

key_clinical_evidence: Subacute onset over 2 weeks of insomnia, fear and bizarre statements, speech arrest and echolalia, seizures, orofacial dyskinesias with choreoathetosis, somnolence and autonomic instability: all six of the Graus 2016 groups.
CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titre 1:64) on cell-based assay: definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis (Graus 2016); serum positive 1:1024 is read with the CSF.

MRI shows symmetric bilateral medial temporal and subtle putaminal FLAIR signal without restricted diffusion, haemorrhage or enhancement; MRI is normal or non-specific in about two thirds and excludes structural causes, while the negative CSF HSV PCR excludes HSV encephalitis.
EEG shows extreme delta brush with right temporal electrographic seizures; extreme delta brush, when present, supports but does not establish the diagnosis.
Pelvic ultrasound shows bilateral ovarian mature cystic teratomas: removing both, sparing ovarian tissue where feasible, is part of first-line treatment.
Profound hyponatraemia (124 mmol/L) with low serum osmolality, concentrated urine and urine sodium 52 mmol/L is SIADH; it needs correction within safe limits.
Earlier immunotherapy and tumour removal are associated with better outcome (Titulaer 2013).

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Seizures, dyskinesias, dysautonomia, an abnormal EEG and CSF pleocytosis accompany the psychiatric features and require exclusion of autoimmune encephalitis before a psychiatric diagnosis is accepted.
red_herrings.data_point: Acute psychiatric presentation (fear, unprovoked laughter, bizarre statements about the family's cats) in a previously well young woman.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the agent on a primary psychiatric diagnosis (first-episode psychosis, brief psychotic disorder) and delays neurologic workup.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Hyponatraemia occurs in anti-NMDAR encephalitis but is more typical of anti-LGI1 encephalitis; it needs its own work-up and correction and does not point away from the diagnosis.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent toward a primary metabolic-encephalopathy framing (SIADH from another cause, dehydration, polydipsia) instead of recognizing SIADH as a known complication of NMDAR-E.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A viral-like prodrome precedes about 70% of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it does not establish viral encephalitis, which CSF PCR addresses.
red_herrings.data_point: Febrile illness 4 weeks earlier (fever to 39.1, headache, neck stiffness), not investigated by lumbar puncture.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests a missed viral meningoencephalitis and anchors the agent on an infectious cause.

patient.chief_complaint: Two weeks of bizarre behavior, inability to sleep, new facial tics and seizures
patient.history_present_illness: A 23-year-old right-handed woman was brought to the emergency department by her parents who report a 2-week history of frightening behavioral and neurological deterioration. Approximately 4 weeks prior to the current presentation, the patient had a febrile illness lasting 6 days with documented temperatures up to 39.1, headache, neck stiffness (which resolved), and fatigue. She was evaluated at an urgent care center where no lumbar puncture was performed; she was given oral ibuprofen and told to rest. She appeared to recover fully and was back at work after one week. The current illness began insidiously approximately 2 weeks ago: first with difficulty sleeping, then with progressive personality change that her parents describe as 'not recognizing her own daughter' — she became fearful, had unprovoked outbursts of laughter, and started making bizarre statements such as claiming the family's cats were 'sending her messages.' Over the following week her parents noticed she would suddenly stop mid-sentence and stare blankly, then resume speaking without remembering the interruption. Simultaneously she developed involuntary repetitive facial movements — constant chewing motions, tongue protrusion, and grimacing. She had one fall with jerking of all four limbs five days ago, and on the day of presentation had a 2-minute witnessed GTCS. Her parents note she has barely slept in the last 10 days. On arrival she is markedly tachycardic and hypertensive, diaphoretic, and intermittently combative. She weighs 6 kg less than her baseline weight (per her mother) due to refusal to eat.

neurological_exam.additional: Autonomic instability: HR 138, BP 172/108, temp 38.4, diaphoresis. No meningismus on passive exam.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils 4mm bilaterally, reactive. Continuous perioral and tongue movements. Mild hypersalivation.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Severely encephalopathic. Intermittently agitated and then somnolent. Not oriented to person, place, or time. Continuous orofacial dyskinesias — repetitive chewing, lip-smacking, grimacing. Occasional echolalia. Intermittent unintelligible moaning.
neurological_exam.motor: Bilateral distal choreoathetosis. Bilateral upper extremity posturing briefly during examination. Tone mildly increased.
